title: Nvidia’s board reportedly prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang as a second affair report sends the stock sliding
summary: Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, with the Wall Street Journal reporting that the board was meeting as soon as Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to determine his future. On Sunday, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy, and on Wednesday evening the New York Times reported he also had an affair with an executive who reports to him. Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down about 11% in the past five days. Huang has said he has about 60 direct reports, and the company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. According to Bloomberg, Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates who could potentially replace Huang as CEO.

title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures slip as Nvidia’s leadership turmoil sours the AI trade
summary: Reuters reported Thursday, November 12, 2026, that futures tracking the Nasdaq 100 led Wall Street lower after reports that Nvidia’s board was weighing the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. At 7:03 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 16 points, or 0.03%, S&P 500 E-minis were down 30.5 points, or 0.4%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 246.25 points, or 0.86%. Chipmakers Intel, Marvell Technology and Micron fell between 2.7% and 3.5%, CoreWeave dropped about 7%, and Nebius edged 0.4% lower ahead of results. The declines threatened to erase Wednesday’s gains, when strong results from CoreWeave helped AI stocks regain some footing. Investors are also awaiting Friday’s Producer Price Index, and traders see a December Federal Reserve rate hike as a certainty, with about a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

title: Nvidia sinks 8% premarket as analysts slash targets while the board weighs Huang’s fate
summary: CNBC reported Nvidia’s stock was down 8.1% in premarket trading as of 7:05 a.m. ET on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after CNBC confirmed the board met on Wednesday to discuss whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang. Several Wall Street analysts told CNBC that if Huang is removed as CEO, the stock could fall 20%, and Nvidia’s stock is already down more than 20% over the last month. Bernstein on Thursday slashed its price target on Nvidia by half, from $400 to $200. Bernstein senior analyst Stacy Rasgon said the alleged affair with a direct report makes it “much tougher for the board to leave him in position.” Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners, said Nvidia’s lack of a succession plan makes the stock “uninvestable.”

title: AMD and Broadcom climb premarket as investors bet Nvidia’s turmoil could help its closest rivals
summary: Investing.com reported that AMD and Broadcom rallied in premarket trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board was preparing to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang. By 5:57 a.m. ET, Nvidia shares had tumbled more than 6%, while AMD and Broadcom rose 3.6% and 2.5%, respectively. AMD’s GPU roadmap competes directly with Nvidia’s data center accelerators, and continued uncertainty at Nvidia could speed cloud providers’ diversification. William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform, saying it sees “an opportunity for AMD to benefit from custom programs as an opportunity for CPU attach.” A source told Reuters the Nvidia board meeting took place Wednesday night, though no official outcome or board statement had been confirmed.

title: Sandisk led the S&P 500 with a 13% jump Wednesday, then slipped premarket as the chip rally cooled
summary: Barchart reported that Wall Street’s three main benchmarks closed higher on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, as upbeat CoreWeave earnings, robust demand for Anthropic’s IPO and record quarterly revenue at OpenAI reignited enthusiasm for the AI trade. Sandisk jumped over 13% to lead S&P 500 gainers, Micron Technology surged more than 11%, and CoreWeave popped over 24% as the top percentage gainer in the Nasdaq 100. In Thursday premarket trading, as turmoil at Nvidia dampened sentiment, Sandisk was down over 4% while Micron and Intel each fell more than 3%. Cisco Systems, Applied Materials, Nebius Group and Cerebras Systems are scheduled to report quarterly results Thursday.

title: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly tops $10 billion for the first time
summary: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources, TechCrunch wrote on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. If true, that would be an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales OpenAI reportedly recorded in the second quarter. Its adjusted operating margin narrowed from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third, the report said. OpenAI has now reached an annual revenue run rate of $50 billion, according to Bloomberg, while Anthropic said its run rate rose by $10 billion within a month to $81 billion as of the end of October. TechCrunch notes the two companies calculate annualized revenue differently.

title: United won’t let personal AI agents book its flights, citing privacy and regulatory concerns
summary: United says it won’t let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing privacy and regulatory concerns, The Verge reported on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, citing the Wall Street Journal. United is concerned that agents could expose customers’ information, make purchases they didn’t intend, and skirt federal rules such as having travelers attest that their bags don’t contain explosives. Agents can still show users United flights but won’t be able to complete the transaction on their behalf. “To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman,” United CEO Scott Kirby said at an event on Tuesday, according to the Journal. United said it could reconsider as third-party agents advance, but wants to make sure it has “established protections for travelers first.”

title: Meta’s longtime infrastructure chief steps down as its AI compute buildout surges
summary: Santosh Janardhan, Meta’s longtime head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, is stepping down, Meta told TechCrunch on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. He will be replaced by Dave Brown, who joined Meta as vice president of infrastructure earlier this year after 19 years at Amazon focused on compute, cloud and AI. A Meta representative said Janardhan will stay on for the transition and move into an advisory role on Meta Compute, and he is expected to leave next year. Janardhan joined the company in 2009, and earlier this year he was tasked with leading Meta Compute, the initiative to scale its data center investments. Bloomberg first reported the departure, citing an internal memo that cited the need to “pass the baton.”

title: Google DeepMind unveils AlphaGenome 2 to predict how DNA changes affect individual cell types
summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2 on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, a successor to its AlphaGenome model designed to predict the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. The model was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues, and DeepMind says it identifies nearly twice as many variants that can change gene expression than its previous state-of-the-art model. Researchers found it could make predictions about new cell types and biological states without retraining and could flag gaps in experimental data. Genomics lead Žiga Avsec said its finer predictions are “more expensive” to produce, so it won’t replace AlphaGenome soon. Google is making AlphaGenome 2 available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API, with a limited private preview for commercial research.

title: Runway opens up Praxis-1, its 27B world action model for robots, under Apache 2.0
summary: Runway made Praxis-1, its world action model for robotics, available to everyone with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Praxis-1 is a 27B-parameter mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer that predicts video and actions together, built on the large-scale video pretraining behind Runway’s world models. Runway says it is the top-performing world action model on NVIDIA’s RoboLab-120 leaderboard, reaching 46.2% success across 1,200 episodes versus 42.9% for FLUX 3 Action, 36.8% for Cosmos3 Nano and 28.0% for π0.5. Fine-tuned on Google’s RT-1 robot, which never appeared in its training data, it reached 80.0% success on SimplerEnv versus 52.4% for the original RT-1 policy. Weights and inference and fine-tuning code are on GitHub and Hugging Face, including for commercial use.

title: Zyphra releases ZONOS3-Mini, an open voice-cloning speech model that runs in real time on phones and in the browser
summary: Zyphra released the weights for ZONOS3-Mini, a compact text-to-speech model that performs zero-shot voice cloning from recordings up to 60 seconds long, mlllm.io reported on November 11, 2026. It can design new voices through age, accent and timbre settings and adjust emotion and delivery down to individual words, and it runs in real time in the browser and on mobile devices without a GPU server. The architecture is an 11-layer mixture-of-experts model with 64 experts, about 800 million shared and roughly 100 million active parameters. Zyphra cites time-to-first-audio under 570 ms in the browser on a Pixel 9, under 150 ms on a MacBook Air M3 and an average of 80 ms on an H100 with 8 parallel requests. The weights are under Apache 2.0, and its claim of ranking first among open TTS models rests on Zyphra’s own internal ZTTS2-Eval benchmark.

title: Britain’s Fractile raises $720 million to ship AI chips with DRAM stacked right on top
summary: Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund, TechCrunch reported on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The round was led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint, at a valuation the British government put at “over £5 billion,” possibly $7 billion, a figure reported by the Financial Times and a Reuters source. Fractile takes a full-stack approach that includes a machine learning compiler to maximize how fast LLMs run on its chips. Its hardware design now stacks DRAM on top of each chip, aiming to bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity that agentic AI has made more pressing. CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that the funding will let the startup “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

title: Databricks pitches its Genie agent as an always-on aide that tells bosses the unvarnished truth
summary: Databricks is pitching its Genie AI agent as an always-on assistant that business leaders can assign a wide range of tasks to complete unsupervised, TechCrunch reported on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. CEO Ali Ghodsi showed how he uses his own agent to analyze weak spots in an employee satisfaction survey, summarize a sales pitch that went poorly and prepare for a podcast interview. With 12,000 employees, Ghodsi said Genie helps surface the bad news he is now unlikely to hear as the big boss, citing Dunbar’s number of 150 stable relationships. “Anyone who has more than 150 employees, which is a lot of companies, a lot of people can get value out of this,” he said. He said costs can be controlled through Databricks’ Unity Gateway, which lets companies set usage limits and swap in cheaper open-weight models.

title: Plurai raises $13 million to make AI agents reliable with self-driving-style simulations
summary: Plurai, a startup founded by former Nexar engineers Ilan Kadar and Elad Levi, said Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that it raised $13 million in seed funding led by Team8, with participation from U&I, Velocity and Mercer, TechCrunch reported. Plurai builds a digital twin of a company’s systems, including the knowledge base and tools an agent will use, then maps the agent’s possible flows to prepare it for edge cases, the same simulation approach used for self-driving cars. The platform works alongside agentic tools like Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Cursor. Kadar says its bigger promise is post-training small open-weight models for individual customers, and tests with Nvidia and Nebius showed its models outperforming midtier frontier models at lower cost. “It is very easy to build a demo, but [hard] to get something that will be reliable and cost effective,” Kadar said.

title: After 51 doctors, a UCLA senior’s TickTracker AI wins a $50,000 HHS prize to fight Lyme disease
summary: UCLA senior Olivia Goodreau, who visited 51 doctors over 18 months before being diagnosed with Lyme disease at age seven, has won a $50,000 Second Place Prize with her TickTracker AI team in the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services TOPx Tech Sprint for AI & Invisible Illness, UCLA Samueli Electrical and Computer Engineering announced on November 11, 2026. The team competed in the Lyme Innovation category. TickTracker AI combines artificial intelligence, federal open data, geospatial mapping and public health information to identify ticks through image recognition and map exposure risks, on a free, multilingual platform. Goodreau also founded the LivLyme Foundation, a nonprofit supporting children battling Lyme disease. “My experience with Lyme disease changed my life, but it also gave me a purpose,” she said.

title: Inspired by a father’s three heart attacks, Bangladeshi students win with an AI stethoscope clip
summary: A team of students from the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh University of Professionals and BRAC University won Grameenphone’s FutureMakers 2026 competition in Dhaka on November 10 with EchoClip, an AI-powered device that attaches to a conventional stethoscope to analyze heart sounds for early signs of heart disease, The Daily Star reported. The idea came from a teammate’s experience with her father’s three heart attacks, and the team trained its model on more than 10,000 publicly available heart recordings. First runner-up River Sentinel built an AI river-erosion prediction system reporting 82% accuracy from satellite data, and Team Jinxed placed third with Spasto AI, a speech therapy app. Held under the theme ‘AI for Social Good,’ the contest drew more than 7,000 students who submitted 1,103 ideas from over 70 universities.

title: LHSAA State Volleyball Championships take over the Cajundome Thursday through Saturday
summary: The LHSAA 2026 State Volleyball Championships run Thursday, November 12, through Saturday, November 14, at the Cajundome. Thursday’s first matches start at 9:00 a.m. with doors at 8 a.m., including Northside Christian vs. Episcopal of Acadiana and, later, Lafayette Christian vs. Isadore Newman and Teurlings Catholic vs. Belle Chasse. Friday’s session starts at 10:00 a.m. and Saturday’s at 9:00 a.m. Only single-day tickets are sold, with no re-entry, and the box office opens one hour before the first game of the day. A clear bag policy is in effect, and all rounds will be broadcast live on the NFHS Network.

title: Free trivia night under the oaks at Moncus Park’s Treehouse tonight
summary: Moncus Park hosts a free evening of trivia with Pigeon Post Trivia on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. at the Treehouse. The park says to gather your crew, flex your brain and see how you stack up. All ages are welcome. The program is free and open to the community. It is the last date on the park’s fall trivia schedule, which also ran September 10 and October 8.

title: Food Truck Friday lunch rolls into Moncus Park
summary: Moncus Park’s Food Truck Friday: Fall Edition returns Friday, November 13, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Visitors can grab lunch from local food trucks, then stay awhile under the oaks with tables inside or out, shade, fans, yard games and room for the kids to play. Trucks are announced each Friday morning on the park’s Facebook page. The fall run continues with one more date on Friday, November 20. Moncus Park parking is $2 an hour Tuesday through Sunday.

title: STEM Saturday at the Lafayette Science Museum: is your Thanksgiving turkey a dinosaur?
summary: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette Science Museum holds STEM Saturday on November 14, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., exploring the paleontology fact that birds are living dinosaurs. Young scientists will investigate what turkeys and dinosaurs have in common, test different “dinosaur beaks” to see which are best at collecting food, and create their own Thanksgiving dinosaur. The activities use clues from bones, feet, feathers and eggs to show how scientists know today’s birds descend from dinosaurs. STEM Saturdays are funded by a grant from Halliburton and are included with regular museum admission. They are geared toward elementary and middle school ages, but all ages are welcome.

title: Acadiana Heart Walk steps off at Moncus Park Saturday afternoon
summary: The Acadiana Heart Walk takes place at Moncus Park on Saturday, November 14, 2026. The event opens at 3:00 p.m., and the walk begins at 4:15 p.m. Registration is open. Moncus Park says joining Heart Walk means joining more than a million people in 300+ cities across America in taking a stand against heart disease. Moncus Park is at 2913 Johnston Street.

title: Girls on the Run 5K brings a medal for every finisher to Moncus Park Sunday
summary: The Girls on the Run 5K comes to Moncus Park in Lafayette on Sunday, November 15, 2026. Inspiration Village opens at 12:45 p.m., and the 5K begins at 2 p.m. The event is non-competitive, and men, women, boys and girls of all ages are invited to join. Every finisher receives a custom Girls on the Run 5K medal, a shirt and post-5K food, with packet pickup at the information table on event day. Registration is open.
